passages.source_text: καὶ δὴ ποτέ τις πρὸς αὐτῷ τῷ ἔτει ἐν φθινοπωρινῇ τροπῇ δημοσία στὰς ἐβόα λέγων Ἄνδρες Ῥωμαῖοι, ἀκούσατε· ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱὸς ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ πάρεστιν, ἐπαγγελλόμενος πᾶσιν τοῖς βουλομένοις ζωὴν αἰώνιον, ἐὰν τὰ κατὰ γνώμην τοῦ πέμψαντος αὐτὸν πατρὸς βιώσωσιν. διὸ μεταβάλλεσθε τὸν τρόπον ἀπὸ τῶν χειρόνων ἐπὶ τὰ κρείττονα, ἀπὸ τῶν προσκαίρων ἐπὶ τὰ αἰώνια· γνῶτε ἕνα θεὸν εἶναι τὸν ἐπουράνιον, οὗ τὸν κόσμον ἀδίκως οἰκεῖτε ἔμπροσθεν τῶν αὐτοῦ δικαίων ὀφθαλμῶν. ἀλλ’ ἐὰν μεταβάλησθε καὶ κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ βούλησιν βιώσητε, εἰς ἕτερον αἰῶνα ἐνεχθέντες καὶ ἀΐδιοι γινόμενοι τῶν ἀπορρήτων αὐτοῦ ἀγαθῶν ἀπολαύσετε· ἐὰν δὲ ἀπειθήσητε, αἱ ψυχαὶ ὑμῶν μετὰ τὴν τοῦ σώματος·λύσιν εἰς τὸν τόπον τοῦ πυρὸς βληθήσονται, ὅπου ἀϊδίως κολαζόμεναι ἀνωφέλητα μετανοήσουσιν· ὁ γὰρ τῆς μετανοίας καιρὸς ἡ νῦν ἑκάστου ζωὴ τυγχάνει. ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν ταῦτα ἀκούων ἠχθόμην ὅτι οὐδεὶς ἐκ τοσούτων ὄχλων τηλικαύτην ἀγγελίαν ἀκούσας εἴρηκεν Εἰς Ἰουδαίαν πορεύσομαι, ἵνα ἴδω εἰ ταῦθ’ οὗτος λέγων ἀληθεύει. ὡς ὅτι υἱὸς θεοῦ ἐπιδεδήμηκεν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ, ἀγαθῆς καὶ αἰωνίας ἐλπίδος χάριν τὴν τοῦ ἀποστείλαντος πατρὸς βούλησιν ἐκφαίνων, ἐπεὶ καὶ ὅπερ λέγουσιν αὐτὸν κηρύσσειν, οὐκ ἔστιν μικρόν· ὧν μὲν γὰρ τὰς ψυχὰς διαβεβαιοῦται αἰωνίους οὔσας αἰωνίων ἀπολαύσειν ἀγαθῶν, ὧν δὲ ἐν πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ ῥιφείσας τὸν αἰῶνα κολασθήσεσθαι.

τοῦ ἑνὸς καὶ μόνου θεοῦ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον πεποιηκότος καὶ ἡμᾶς κτίσαντος καὶ πάντα παρεσχηκότος τοιαύτη πέφυκεν φύσις, παντὸς οὐδήποτε ἐντὸς ὅρων θεοσεβείας ὄντος καὶ μὴ βλασφημοῦντος αὐτοῦ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα, στοργῇ τῇ πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰς αὐτὸν φέρειν τὴν ψυχήν, ἐμφύτου εἰς αὐτὸν ἔρωτος · ἰδέᾳ. κἂν ἁμαρτωλὸς ᾖ, μετὰ τὸ κατ’ ἀξίαν ὧν ἔπραξεν κολασθῆναι σώζεσθαι φύσιν ἔχει. εἰ δέ τις αὐτὸν ἀρνήσεται ἢ ἑτέρως πως λόγῳ εἰς αὐτὸν ἀσεβήσει, ἔπειτα μετανοήσει, κολασθήσεται μὲν ἐφ’ ὧν εἰς αὐτὸν ἥμαρτεν, σωθήσεται δέ, ὅτι ἐπιστρέψας ἠγάπησεν. ἴσως δέ, εἰ τῆς εὐσεβείας ὑπερβολὴ καὶ τῆς ἱκεσίας ᾖ, καὶ τοῦ κολασθῆναι ἀπολυθήσεται, συγγνώμης τῆς ἁμαρτίας μετὰ τῆς μετανοίας δεδωκὼς τὴν ἄγνοιαν. οἱ δὲ μὴ μετανοήσαντες διὰ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς κολάσεως καὶ τὸ τέλος ἕξουσιν, κἂν ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἅπασιν ὁσιώτατοι ὦσιν· ἀλλ’ ὡς ἔφην, μεμετρημένου αἰῶνος τὸ πέμπτον πυρὶ αἰωνίῳ κολασθέντες ἀποσβεσθήσονται. εἶναι γὰρ εἰς ἀεὶ οὐκέτι δύνανται οἱ εἰς τὸν ἀεὶ καὶ μόνον ἀσεβήσαντες θεόν.

αὐτίκα γοῦν ἐγὼ τὴν πᾶσαν Ἑλλήνων παιδείαν κακοῦ δαίμονος χαλεπωτάτην ὑπόθεσιν εἶναι λέγω. οἱ μὲν γὰρ αὐτῶν πολλοὺς θεοὺς εἰσηγήσαντο, καὶ τούτους κακοὺς καὶ παντοπαθεῖς, ἵνα ὁ τὰ ὅμοια πράττειν θέλων μηδὲ αἰδῆται (ὅπερ ἐστὶν ἀνθρώπου ἴδιον), παράδειγμα ἔχων τῶν μυθολογουμένων θεῶν τοὺς κακοὺς καὶ ἀσέμνους βίους. τῷ δὲ μηδὲ αἰδεῖσθαι οὐδὲ ἐλπίδα μετανοίας ὁ τοιοῦτος ἐμφαίνει. ἄλλοι δὲ εἱμαρμένην εἰσηγήσαντο, τὴν λεγομένην γένεσιν, παρ’ ἣν μηδένα πάσχειν τι ἢ ποιεῖν δύνασθαι. ὁμοίως οὖν καὶ τοῦτο τῷ πρώτῳ ταὐτόν ἐστιν· νομίσας γάρ τις ὅτι παρὰ γένεσιν οὐδεὶς οὔτε πάσχειν οὔτε ποιεῖν ἔχει, ῥᾳδίως ἐπὶ τὸ ἁμαρτάνειν ἔρχεται — καὶ ἁμαρτὼν οὐ μεταμελεῖται ἐφ’ οἷς ἠσέβηκεν, ἀπολογίαν φέρων ὅτι ὑπὸ γενέσεως αὐτὰ ποιεῖν ἐξηναγκάζετο — καὶ ὡς τὴν γένεσιν κατορθῶσαι μὴ δυνάμενος, ἐφ’ οἷς ἐξαμαρτάνει οὐδὲ τὸ αἰδεῖσθαι ἔχει.

ἄλλοι δὲ ἀπρονόητον φορὰν εἰσηγοῦνται, ὡς. αὐτομάτως τῶν πάντων περιφερομένων, οὐδενὸς ἐφεστηκότος δεσπότου. ταῦτα δὲ οὕτω νομίζειν, ὡς εἰρήκαμεν, πασῶν δοξῶν τυγχάνει οὖσα χαλεπωτάτη. ὡς γὰρ οὐκ ὄντος τοῦ ἐφεστῶτος καὶ προνοουμένου καὶ ἑκάστῳ τὸ κατ’ ἀξίαν ἀπονέμοντος, πᾶν ὅ,τι δύναται διὰ τὴν ἀφοβίαν εὐκόλως δράσει. ὅθεν οὐ ῥᾳδίως (ἢ τάχα οὐδὲ ὅλως) οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα φρονοῦντες σωφρονίζονται· τὸν γὰρ ἐπιστρέφοντα κίνδυνον οὐ προορῶνται. ὁ δὲ τῶν (ὡς ὑμεῖς φατέ) βαρβάρων Ἰουδαίων λόγος εὐσεβέστατός ἐστιν, ἕνα πατέρα καὶ δημιουργὸν τοῦδε τοῦ παντὸς εἰσηγούμενος, τῇ φύσει ἀγαθὸν καὶ δίκαιον· ἀγαθὸν μὲν ὡς μεταμελομένοις χαριζόμενον τὰ ἁμαρτήματα, δίκαιον δὲ ὡς ἑκάστῳ μετὰ τὴν μετάνοιαν κατ’ ἀξίαν τῶν πεπραγμένων ἐπεξιόντα.

διὰ τοῦτο πρῶτον ὑπὸ τοῦ προδρόμου Σίμωνος προαπατηθέντες, θεῷ τὰς ψυχὰς ἀπεθάνετε καὶ τὰ σώματα ἐπατάχθητε· δύνασθε δὲ ὁμοίως τὸ δεύτερον, διὰ τῆς μετανοίας (ὡς ἔφην) τὰ θεῷ ἀρέσκοντα ἀναδεξάμενοι καὶ τὰ σώματα ἀναρρῶσαι καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἀναλαβεῖν. ἔστιν δὲ τὰ ἀρέσκοντα τῷ θεῷ τὸ αὐτῷ προσεύχεσθαι, αὐτὸν αἰτεῖν ὡς πάντα νόμῳ κριτικῷ διδόντα, „τραπέζης δαιμόνων“ ἀπέχεσθαι, νεκρᾶς μὴ γεύεσθαι σαρκός, μὴ ψαύειν αἵματος, ἐκ παντὸς ἀπολούεσθαι λύματος. τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ ἐνὶ λόγῳ ὡς οἱ θεὸν σέβοντες ἤκουσαν Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ ὑμεῖς ἀκούσατε ἅπαντες, ἐν πολλοῖς σώμασιν μίαν γνώμην ἀναλαβόντες Ἅπερ ἕκαστος ἑαυτῷ βούλεται καλά, τὰ αὐτὰ βουλευέσθω καὶ τῷ πλησίον. οὕτω δ’ ἂν ὑμῶν ἕκαστος νοήσειεν τὸ καλόν, εἰ ἑαυτῷ διαλεχθείη τὰ τοιαῦτα Οὐ θέλεις φονευθῆναι, ἕτερον μὴ φονεύσῃς· οὐ θέλεις τὴν σὴν ὑφ’ ἑτέρου μοιχευθῆναι γυναῖκα, τὴν ἑτέρου μὴ μοίχευε γαμετήν· οὐ θέλεις τι τῶν σῶν κλαπῆναι, ἑτέρου μὴ κλέπτε μηδέν. καὶ οὕτως ἀφ’ ὑμῶν αὐτῶν τὸ εὔλογον συννοοῦντες καὶ ποιοῦντες, θεῷ προσφιλεῖς γενόμενοι, ἐπιτεύξεσθε τῆς ἰάσεως, ἐπεὶ καὶ ἐν τῷ παρόντι αἰῶνι βασανισθήσεσθε τὰ σώματα καὶ ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι κολασθήσεσθε τὰς ψυχάς.

τοιαῦτα ὑπὸ τοῦ Πέτρου ἐν ὀλίγαις ἡμέραις κατηχηθέντες καὶ ἰαθέντες ἐβαπτίσθησαν, ἔπειτα τοῖς λοιποῖς αὐτοῦ θαύμασιν περίλυποι πάντες ἐν μέσαις ταῖς ἀγοραῖς πανδημεὶ ἐπὶ σποδοῦ καὶ σάκκου ἐκαθέζοντο, μετανοοῦντες ἐπὶ τοῖς πρότερον ἡμαρτημένοις. καὶ οἱ ἐν Σιδῶνι ταῦτα ἀκούσαντες τὰ ὅμοια ἐποίησαν, καὶ ἱκέτας πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον ἀπέστελλον ὡς αὐτοὶ διὰ τὰς νόσους πρὸς αὐτὸν ἐλθεῖν μὴ δυνάμενοι. ὁ Πέτρος δὲ ἡμερῶν οὐ πολλῶν ἐνδιατρίψας τῇ Τύρῳ καὶ κατηχήσας τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ ἅπαντας καὶ παντοδαπῶν αὐτοὺς ἀπαλλάξας παθῶν, ἐκκλησίαν τε συστησάμενος καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν ἑπομένων αὐτῷ πρεσβυτέρων ἐπίσκοπον αὐτοῖς καταστήσας ὥρμησεν εἰς Σιδῶνα. ὁ δὲ Σίμων μαθὼν ἥκοντα τὸν Πέτρον εὐθὺς ἀπέδρα εἰς Βηρυτὸν μετὰ Ἀππίωνος καὶ τῶν αὐτοῦ ἑταίρων.

translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | repent / repentance where context supports moral-spiritual change | change of mind, reconsider, regret and other contextual renderings | See "Repentance terminology (2026-10-13)"; explain the meaning without homogenizing distinct source expressions |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Repentance terminology (2026-10-13)

The contextual reassessment supersedes the October 11 reorientation default.
Use **repent / repentance** for the moral-spiritual response where the passage
supports it. Familiarity alone is not evidence of accuracy; explain the intended
change of disposition and conduct rather than reducing repentance to sadness
or a change of opinion. Reorientation can explain the concept but is not a
mandatory replacement in reader text. No claim about measured reader reception
or independent scholarly approval is made.

**Context still controls.** Retain regret, remorse, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where those fit the source and local direction.
Preserve contested readings in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17, the alternate turning
reading in Jeremiah 31:19, and distinct turn/return verbs in Acts 3:19 and 26:20.
Use "repentance toward God" in Acts 20:21 because the sentence explicitly gives
that direction; do not insert it into every occurrence of metanoia.

Keep sorrow and repentance distinct in 2 Corinthians 7:9-10. Retain the
relationship between repentance and its fruits, rather than equating the two.
Use "I repent" in Luke 17:4 without requiring proof of completed reform before
forgiveness. Preserve baptismal grammar without deciding symbolic versus causal
interpretations by a vocabulary substitution.

Do not add intensifiers. Keep source-backed emphasis such as the existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" in Hermas 21:4. Keep the corrected
"more joy ... than" in Luke 15:7. Extra-canonical writers retain their own
conceptual frameworks, including adverse changes of mind; do not harmonize
them to a canonical Godward formula. Historical English witnesses and source
transcriptions remain untouched; reader adaptations retain their disclosure.

All **397** previously changed records have an explicit new decision, including
retained exceptions and the four October 12 follow-up records. Earlier wording,
notes, plans, and review history are preserved rather than erased. See the
[full decision ledger](docs/REPENTANCE_REASSESSMENT_2026-10-13.md) and exact,
hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/repentance-contextual-2026-10-13.json`.
These remain editorial drafts, not independent scholarly certifications.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.
ambiguity_standard: Apply the supplied DOCTRINE.md ambiguity policy: a defensible contextual rendering may be used in the main text when material alternatives and the reason for the choice are preserved in notes. A unique or uncontested interpretation is not required. Distinguish (a) an unreadable or unverified source, omitted content, invented restoration, or a construction for which no defensible English can be given, from (b) ordinary lexical, attachment, or referent ambiguity faithfully preserved in English or explained with viable alternatives. The former blocks publication; the latter does not automatically block it. A note cannot excuse unsupported wording: the proposed main rendering must itself be defensible from the supplied Greek. Clearly printed gaps must remain gaps, not be filled by invention. Never change a verdict merely to achieve acceptance.
selected_edition_coverage_standard: Coverage is assessed against ALL SURVIVING WORDING AND PRINTED GAP MARKERS in the selected image-checked edition, not against unavailable words of a hypothetical complete original. A confirmed printed lacuna must remain an explicit gap in the English, retaining the exact number of printed dots (layout whitespace may differ), with a source-quoted note explaining that its content is unavailable and no restoration has been supplied. Such faithful representation can pass selected-edition coverage; it must never be described as recovery of the lost wording or an unbroken original. Distinguish this from missing scan pages, unverified ink, omitted surviving Greek, an unsupported English completion, or a translation that obscures the gap: those remain blocking. Neither this scope clarification nor a prior suggestion is an instruction to accept a draft; independently check every surviving clause, every gap, and every disclosure.
authorization: Human approved Codex translators and independently checked public-domain Greek source corrections; originals must be preserved in notes and fresh independent Sol6.1 review is mandatory
curation_pin_status: New source curations pending Git pin; final export must bind their actual canonical commit

And indeed, once in that very year, at the autumn equinox, someone stood up publicly and shouted, saying, “Men of Rome, listen! The Son of God is present in Judea, promising eternal life to all who desire it, if they live according to the intention of the Father who sent him. Therefore change your way—from worse things to better, from temporary things to eternal. Recognize that there is one God, the heavenly one, whose world you inhabit unjustly before his righteous eyes. But if you make this change and live according to his will, you will be carried into another age, become everlasting, and enjoy his ineffable good things. If, however, you disobey, your souls will be cast, after the dissolution of the body, into the place of fire, where, while being punished eternally, they will reorient themselves to no avail. For each person’s present life is the time for reorientation.”

As I listened to this, I was distressed that no one from among such great crowds, after hearing so momentous an announcement, had said, “I will travel to Judea so that I may see whether this man is telling the truth when he says these things.” For the claim was that the Son of God had come to Judea and, for the sake of a good and eternal hope, was revealing the will of the Father who sent him—especially since what they say he proclaims is no small matter. For he confidently affirms that the souls of some, being eternal, will enjoy eternal good things, while the souls of others, cast into unquenchable fire, will be punished throughout the age.

source_issues.issue: The printed middle dot falls inside the article-genitive-noun phrase and interrupts “the dissolution of the body.” The translation provisionally treats it as intrusive editorial punctuation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: in that very year
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase locates the event at or close upon the same year. “About that same year” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: at the autumn equinox
lexical_decisions.rationale: As with the corresponding spring expression, τροπή denotes a seasonal turning point; “at the turn of autumn” is a broader alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: change your way
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording calls for a change in manner or way of life. It is kept distinct from the μετανοέω word group later in the passage.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀνωφέλητα μετανοήσουσιν· ὁ γὰρ τῆς μετανοίας καιρὸς
lexical_decisions.chosen: they will reorient themselves to no avail. For … the time for reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The cognate verb and noun are rendered consistently under the supplied terminology policy. “They will repent uselessly … the time for repentance” is the traditional alternative; “they will regret it to no avail” would emphasize their futile response under punishment.

lexical_decisions.chosen: his ineffable good things
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπόρρητος can mean secret, forbidden to disclose, or unutterable. “Ineffable” fits the transcendent benefits here while preserving their unspeakable character.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὡς ὅτι υἱὸς θεοῦ ἐπιδεδήμηκεν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: For the claim was that the Son of God had come to Judea
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς ὅτι can introduce reported content or give a causal explanation. The context of a public report favors reported content; “since indeed the Son of God had come” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the Son of God
lexical_decisions.rationale: Although the phrase is anarthrous here, it refers contextually to the previously identified ὁ τοῦ θεοῦ υἱός. “A son of God” remains grammatically possible if the phrase is read indefinitely.

lexical_decisions.chosen: will be punished throughout the age
lexical_decisions.rationale: This preserves the explicit noun αἰών rather than automatically assimilating it to the nearby ἀϊδίως. In this context “will be punished forever” is also semantically supportable.

previous_passages.text: The nature of the one and only God, who made the world, created us, and provided everything, is naturally such that, whenever anyone at all is within the bounds of reverence for God and does not blaspheme his holy spirit, it carries that person’s soul toward him by affection for him, in the form of an innate longing for him. Even if that person is a sinner, after being punished as his deeds deserve, it is in his nature to be saved. If someone denies him or in some other way speaks impiously against him, then reorients himself, he will indeed be punished for the ways in which he sinned against him, but he will be saved, because after turning back he loved him. Perhaps, however, if there is an extraordinary degree of reverence and supplication, he will even be released from punishment, having presented his ignorance together with his reorientation as grounds for forgiveness of the sin. Those, however, who have not reoriented themselves will also meet their end through the punishment of fire, even if they are most devout in every other respect. But, as I said, after being punished with age-long fire for one fifth of a measured age, they will be extinguished. For those who have acted impiously against the eternal and only God can no longer exist forever.

source_issues.source_quote: παντὸς οὐδήποτε ἐντὸς ὅρων θεοσεβείας ὄντος
source_issues.issue: The selected print has smooth-breathed οὐδήποτε, which ordinarily means “never” and does not fit the genitive construction with παντός and ὄντος. The translation provisionally understands it as the genitive indefinite οὑδήποτε, “of anyone whatsoever.” This is a proposed interpretation of a confirmed printed orthographic oddity, not a claim that the print was unverified.
source_issues.proposed_reading: παντὸς οὑδήποτε ἐντὸς ὅρων θεοσεβείας ὄντος

source_issues.issue: The confirmed printed raised dot interrupts the natural construction in which ἰδέᾳ governs the preceding genitive phrase. Treating it as sentence-final would leave ἰδέᾳ isolated before the full stop. The translation therefore provisionally treats the raised dot as anomalous internal editorial punctuation and attaches ἰδέᾳ to the preceding words.

lexical_decisions.chosen: is naturally such
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the repeated nature language of πέφυκεν and φύσις while allowing the following infinitive to express what this nature characteristically does.

lexical_decisions.chosen: his holy spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the possessive expression and descriptive wording without using English capitalization to settle personhood beyond what the Greek itself marks.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μετὰ τὸ κατ’ ἀξίαν ὧν ἔπραξεν κολασθῆναι σώζεσθαι φύσιν ἔχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: after being punished as his deeds deserve, it is in his nature to be saved
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατ’ ἀξίαν expresses punishment corresponding to the worth or deserts of the deeds, while φύσιν ἔχει continues the passage’s emphasis on nature.

lexical_decisions.chosen: reorients himself
lexical_decisions.rationale: The verb denotes moral-spiritual redirection here. No destination is added because God has already been named, and the distinct ἐπιστρέψας is separately rendered “after turning back.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: συγγνώμης τῆς ἁμαρτίας μετὰ τῆς μετανοίας δεδωκὼς τὴν ἄγνοιαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: having presented his ignorance together with his reorientation as grounds for forgiveness of the sin
lexical_decisions.rationale: The compact construction presents ignorance and reorientation in relation to pardon. It may alternatively be understood as offering ignorance as an excuse for the sin, but the chosen wording preserves both elements without making ignorance itself absolve him.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μεμετρημένου αἰῶνος τὸ πέμπτον πυρὶ αἰωνίῳ κολασθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: after being punished with age-long fire for one fifth of a measured age
lexical_decisions.rationale: “Age-long” preserves the relation between αἰωνίῳ and αἰῶνος and fits the explicitly measured duration. “Eternal fire” is a possible lexical alternative, in which case the fire rather than each person’s punishment would be described as eternal.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they will be extinguished
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the image of something being put out rather than replacing it with an interpretive abstraction such as “annihilated.”

previous_passages.text: For example, then, I say that the entire education of the Greeks is a most pernicious scheme of an evil demon. Some of them introduced many gods, and these evil and subject to every passion, so that anyone wishing to do similar things might not even feel shame—shame being characteristic of a human being—since he has as his example the evil and indecent lives of the gods spoken of in myth. And by not even feeling shame, such a person does not even show hope of reorientation. Others introduced fate, the so-called nativity, contrary to which no one can experience or do anything. So this too is likewise the same as the first position. For when someone has come to believe that no one is able either to experience or to do anything contrary to nativity, he readily comes to sin—and after sinning he does not regret what he has done impiously, offering as a defense that he was forced by nativity to do these things—and, since he is unable to correct his nativity, he is not even capable of feeling shame for the ways in which he sins.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὴν πᾶσαν Ἑλλήνων παιδείαν κακοῦ δαίμονος χαλεπωτάτην ὑπόθεσιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: the entire education of the Greeks is a most pernicious scheme of an evil demon
lexical_decisions.rationale: παιδεία denotes the Greek system of education or culture, while ὑπόθεσις here is understood as an underlying scheme or design; “most grievous undertaking” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: subject to every passion
lexical_decisions.rationale: The word characterizes the gods as undergoing or being governed by every kind of passion, not merely as suffering greatly.

lexical_decisions.chosen: shame being characteristic of a human being
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὅπερ is taken as referring to the immediately relevant act of feeling shame; reference to the broader preceding clause is grammatically possible but less fitting in context.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ δὲ μηδὲ αἰδεῖσθαι οὐδὲ ἐλπίδα μετανοίας ὁ τοιοῦτος ἐμφαίνει
lexical_decisions.chosen: And by not even feeling shame, such a person does not even show hope of reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The paired μηδέ and οὐδέ are represented by the repeated “not even.” μετάνοια denotes prospective moral redirection here; the traditional alternative is “repentance,” and no Godward destination is added because the clause does not specify one.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the so-called nativity
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this argument γένεσις is the astrologically determined condition associated with one’s birth, not simply the event of birth; “birth-destiny” is an explanatory alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: παρ’ ἣν μηδένα πάσχειν τι ἢ ποιεῖν δύνασθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: contrary to which no one can experience or do anything
lexical_decisions.rationale: παρά with the accusative is read as “contrary to” or “outside the determination of”; “apart from which” is a viable alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: since he is unable to correct his nativity
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατορθόω can mean set right, correct, or successfully master. “Correct” preserves the text’s deliberately impossible task without replacing it with an explanatory paraphrase.

previous_passages.text: Others propose a motion devoid of providence, as though all things revolved spontaneously, with no master presiding over them. To think this way about these matters, as we have said, is in fact the most pernicious of all beliefs. For, as though there were no one presiding, exercising providence, and assigning to each person what is deserved, someone will readily do everything he can because of his lack of fear. Hence those who think such things are not easily—or perhaps not at all—brought to self-restraint, for they do not foresee the danger that would turn them back. But the teaching of the barbarian Jews, as you call them, is most pious, proposing one Father and Creator of this universe, good and just by nature: good, in that he forgives the sins of those who regret them; and just, in that after the reorientation he proceeds against each person according to what the things done deserve.

source_issues.issue: The image-checked printed period after ὡς interrupts a construction in which ὡς appears to introduce the following description. The translation provisionally treats the stop as editorial punctuation rather than as the end of an independent sentence.

source_issues.source_quote: ταῦτα δὲ οὕτω νομίζειν, ὡς εἰρήκαμεν, πασῶν δοξῶν τυγχάνει οὖσα χαλεπωτάτη
source_issues.issue: The feminine forms οὖσα χαλεπωτάτη do not formally agree with the neuter infinitival clause ταῦτα ... νομίζειν. The sentence remains intelligible as an anacoluthon or as attraction to an understood feminine δόξα, “belief,” but no unique grammatical repair is certain.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a motion devoid of providence
lexical_decisions.rationale: φορά can denote motion, course, or movement; the following description of everything revolving spontaneously favors cosmic “motion.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: because of his lack of fear
lexical_decisions.rationale: This avoids the potentially positive connotations of English “fearlessness” and expresses the absence of deterrent fear intended by the argument.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the danger that would turn them back
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπιστρέφοντα is taken transitively, with the affected persons understood. “The returning danger” or “the danger coming back upon them” is also grammatically possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he forgives the sins of those who regret them
lexical_decisions.rationale: χαρίζομαι with sins means freely remit or forgive them. μεταμέλομαι is rendered with regret rather than the distinct reorientation terminology used for μετάνοια.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after the reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The temporal force of μετά is retained, even though this wording creates tension with the preceding statement about forgiveness. Alternatives include “after the change of mind” and the traditional “after repentance”; it is not rewritten as “if there is no reorientation.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἑκάστῳ ... κατ’ ἀξίαν τῶν πεπραγμένων ἐπεξιόντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: he proceeds against each person according to what the things done deserve
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπεξέρχομαι with the dative can mean proceed against, pursue, or call someone to account. “Proceeds against” retains its judicial and potentially punitive force without supplying a different verb such as “reward.”

previous_passages.text: For this reason, after first being deceived by Simon the forerunner, you died to God in your souls, and your bodies were struck. But in the same way you can, a second time, through reorientation—as I said—accept the things pleasing to God and both restore your bodies to health and recover your souls. What pleases God is this: to pray to him; to make requests of him as the one who gives everything according to a judicial law; to abstain from “the table of demons”; not to taste dead flesh; not to touch blood; and to wash oneself clean of every pollution. As for the rest, hear it, all of you, in one saying, just as the Jews who revere God have heard it, taking up one mind in many bodies: “Whatever good things each person wants for himself, he should plan the same things for his neighbor as well.” Each of you would understand what is good in this way, if he were to reason with himself as follows: “You do not want to be murdered; do not murder another. You do not want another to commit adultery with your wife; do not commit adultery with another man’s wedded wife. You do not want any of your possessions to be stolen; do not steal anything belonging to another.” And so, recognizing from your own case what is reasonable and doing it, you will become dear to God and obtain healing; for otherwise you will be tormented in your bodies in the present age and punished in your souls in the age to come.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after first being deceived by Simon the forerunner
lexical_decisions.rationale: πρόδρομος explicitly calls Simon a forerunner, while προαπατάω presents the deception as prior; the translation does not specify whose forerunner he is.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context concerns moral and spiritual redirection expressed by accepting what pleases God. “Through repentance” is the traditional alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τὰ σώματα ἀναρρῶσαι καὶ τὰς ψυχὰς ἀναλαβεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: both restore your bodies to health and recover your souls
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀναρρωννύω denotes renewed bodily strength, while ἀναλαμβάνω here presents the souls as regained or recovered; “take up your souls again” would be more formally literal.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: αὐτὸν αἰτεῖν ὡς πάντα νόμῳ κριτικῷ διδόντα
lexical_decisions.chosen: to make requests of him as the one who gives everything according to a judicial law
lexical_decisions.rationale: κριτικός can mean discriminating or judicial. “According to a law of discernment” is possible, but the surrounding emphasis on consequences and punishment favors “judicial.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: not to taste dead flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: The wording directly prohibits tasting flesh that is dead; it has not been generalized to a familiar dietary formula.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐν πολλοῖς σώμασιν μίαν γνώμην ἀναλαβόντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: taking up one mind in many bodies
lexical_decisions.rationale: The rendering retains the author’s image of bodily plurality united in a single judgment or disposition.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ θέλεις τὴν σὴν ὑφ’ ἑτέρου μοιχευθῆναι γυναῖκα, τὴν ἑτέρου μὴ μοίχευε γαμετήν
lexical_decisions.chosen: You do not want another to commit adultery with your wife; do not commit adultery with another man’s wedded wife
lexical_decisions.rationale: The English changes the first clause from passive to active to avoid implying sexual coercion while preserving the participants and the repeated adultery terminology. The distinction between γυναῖκα, “wife,” and γαμετήν, “wedded wife,” is also retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπεὶ καὶ ἐν τῷ παρόντι αἰῶνι βασανισθήσεσθε
lexical_decisions.chosen: for otherwise you will be tormented in your bodies in the present age
lexical_decisions.rationale: After an exhortation or stated favorable outcome, ἐπεί can introduce the consequence that follows otherwise. The formally possible “since indeed you will be tormented” would obscure the warning contrast supplied by the context.

previous_passages.text: After being instructed in such things by Peter over a few days and being healed, they were baptized. Then, all deeply grieved by his further wonders, they sat together as a whole populace in the middle of the marketplaces on ashes and sackcloth, reorienting themselves over the sins they had previously committed. When those in Sidon heard these things, they did the same and sent suppliants to Peter, since they themselves were unable to come to him because of their diseases. Peter, after staying in Tyre for not many days, instructing everyone in it, freeing them from every kind of affliction, forming a church, and appointing for them a bishop from among the elders who followed him, set out for Sidon. On learning that Peter was coming, Simon immediately fled to Beirut with Appion and his companions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τοιαῦτα ὑπὸ τοῦ Πέτρου ἐν ὀλίγαις ἡμέραις κατηχηθέντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: After being instructed in such things by Peter over a few days
lexical_decisions.rationale: κατηχέω here means to instruct orally; “catechized” would preserve the later technical term but would be less accessible in modern English.

lexical_decisions.chosen: deeply grieved by his further wonders
lexical_decisions.rationale: περίλυπος takes the dative as the cause or occasion of grief, and λοιπός can mean remaining, other, or further. “Deeply grieved at his other wonders” is a close alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πανδημεὶ ἐπὶ σποδοῦ καὶ σάκκου ἐκαθέζοντο
lexical_decisions.chosen: they sat together as a whole populace ... on ashes and sackcloth
lexical_decisions.rationale: πανδημεί means collectively or with the whole populace, while ἐπί with the genitive presents ashes and sackcloth as what they sat upon.

lexical_decisions.chosen: reorienting themselves over the sins they had previously committed
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle describes moral reorientation in response to earlier sins, while ἐπί identifies those sins as its occasion. “Repenting over their former sins” is the traditional alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: forming a church
lexical_decisions.rationale: In the context of appointing a bishop from among elders, ἐκκλησία denotes an organized congregation or church, and συνίστημι denotes forming or establishing it.

lexical_decisions.chosen: On learning that Peter was coming
lexical_decisions.rationale: In the narrative sequence Peter has just set out for Sidon, so the present participle is best understood as his approach. Because ἥκω can also have a perfect-like sense, “had arrived” remains grammatically possible.

revision_evidence.reason: Maintainer-approved October13 contextual repentance policy supersedes October11 reorientation default; actual new source review is required for every audited main-text hit, including explicit contextual exceptions
